evidence.text: AD2 In the past four weeks, have you seen or heard any advertising for each of these brands?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Yes; 0 No; 9 Not sure. Blank if unaware. Derive adrecall_bXX all-sample 1 only for Yes, 0 otherwise. Report Not sure separately. Recall is not verified exposure or campaign effectiveness.

evidence.text: W1 Thinking about what other people have said about [BRAND] in the past four weeks, what have you heard?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Mainly positive; 2 Mainly negative; 3 A mixture of positive and negative; 4 Neutral comments; 5 Have not heard people talk about it. Blank if unaware. Retain all five categories; do not disguise mixed or neutral as not heard.

evidence.text: P1 Which of the following have you used in the past seven days?
following: Response: Multiple response checklist. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: One binary variable per medium; None exclusive. This is personal media use, not advertising exposure or a channel-effectiveness metric.

evidence.text: A1 When you think of passenger car brands available in South Africa, which brand comes to mind first?
following: Response: Open text. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: Record verbatim before any names are shown. Code to brand registry; 96 Other named brand; 98 None. Do not correct or suggest brands.

evidence.text: A2 What other passenger car brands come to mind? Please name any others you can think of.
following: Response: Open text with multiple mentions. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: Record verbatim and code every distinct brand. Derive unaided_bXX including A1 and A2. No fixed minimum. 0 Not recalled; 1 Recalled for each tracked brand.

evidence.text: A3 Before today, which of these brands had you heard of?
following: Response: Multiple response brand list. Ask: all eligible.

Codes and programming: aware_bXX: 0 No; 1 Yes. Include recognised spontaneous or CEP recalls. If a brand was named earlier but not selected now, clarify neutrally before finalising. aware_none is exclusive. Keep resolved recognition separate from the original open responses.

evidence.text: F1 If you were choosing your next vehicle, which of these brands would you consider buying or leasing?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: all eligible; show recognised brands.
Codes and programming: consider_bXX: 0 Not considered; 1 Considered. None allowed. These are intentions at the interview, not observed future purchases.

evidence.text: F2 Which of those brands would make your serious shortlist?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: F1 has any selected brand; show only F1 selections.
Codes and programming: shortlist_bXX: 0 No; 1 Yes. Allow no shortlist yet. Do not force a top three.

evidence.text: F3 Which one of your shortlisted brands would be your first choice?
following: Response: Single response. Ask: F2 has any selected brand.

Codes and programming: Brand code 1–10; 98 No first choice yet. Derive firstchoice_bXX. Nested funnel: awareness >= consideration >= shortlist >= first choice. Not a longitudinal conversion or causal probability.

coverage.note: O4 repeat_bXX asks prior household acquisition only among brands acquired in the last 12 months. It is not an all-respondent ever-used/trial grid.
No per-brand past-week/month/3-month/6-month use grid. Do not substitute current ownership or acquisition.

evidence.text: O1 Which brands of vehicle does your household currently own or lease?

evidence.text: O3 Which brands has your household bought or started leasing in the past 12 months?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: S3=1.

Codes and programming: bought12_bXX 0/1; bought12_other 0/1. Rest of sample gets structural zero for derived all-sample indicators. Record asked route in S3. Acquisition can be new, used or lease, not a national new-car sales estimate.

coverage.note: bought12_b01–b10 / O3 is past-12-month acquisition, not usage or ownership over that window. owner_b01–b10 / O1 is current ownership.

evidence.text: AD1 Which car brands, if any, have you seen or heard advertising for in the past four weeks?
following: Response: Open text with multiple mentions. Ask: all eligible.

Codes and programming: Record verbatim, code ad_unaided_bXX 0/1. This occurs after brand recognition, so label it unprompted advertising recall after brand-list exposure, not uncontaminated top-of-mind awareness.

evidence.text: AD2 In the past four weeks, have you seen or heard any advertising for each of these brands?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Yes; 0 No; 9 Not sure. Blank if unaware. Derive adrecall_bXX all-sample 1 only for Yes, 0 otherwise. Report Not sure separately. Recall is not verified exposure or campaign effectiveness.

evidence.text: W1 Thinking about what other people have said about [BRAND] in the past four weeks, what have you heard?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Mainly positive; 2 Mainly negative; 3 A mixture of positive and negative; 4 Neutral comments; 5 Have not heard people talk about it. Blank if unaware. Retain all five categories; do not disguise mixed or neutral as not heard.

evidence.text: P1 Which of the following have you used in the past seven days?
following: Response: Multiple response checklist. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: One binary variable per medium; None exclusive. This is personal media use, not advertising exposure or a channel-effectiveness metric.

evidence.text: S1 How old are you?
following: Response: Numeric. Ask: all.
Codes and programming: 18–69 eligible. Record exact age and derive age band. Otherwise end.

evidence.text: Codes and programming: 18–69 eligible. Record exact age and derive age band. Otherwise end.
D1 How do you describe your gender?
following: Response: Single response. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: 1 Man; 2 Woman; 3 Another identity; 4 Prefer not to say. Do not force binary coding.

evidence.text: D4 What is your total monthly household income before tax?
following: Response: Single response. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: 1 Below R15,000; 2 R15,000–R29,999; 3 R30,000–R49,999; 4 R50,000–R79,999; 5 R80,000 or more; 99 Prefer not to say. Use 99 as nonresponse in income summaries.

evidence.text: Codes and programming: 1 Below R15,000; 2 R15,000–R29,999; 3 R30,000–R49,999; 4 R50,000–R79,999; 5 R80,000 or more; 99 Prefer not to say. Use 99 as nonresponse in income summaries.
O5 Where did your household obtain its most recently acquired vehicle?
following: Response: Single response. Ask: S3=1.

Codes and programming: 1 Authorised dealer; 2 Independent used-car dealer; 3 Private seller; 4 Online marketplace; 5 Direct online from manufacturer; 6 Auction; 7 Other. Channels must sum to 100% among recent acquirers. Blank for others.

evidence.text: A3 Before today, which of these brands had you heard of?
following: Response: Multiple response brand list. Ask: all eligible.

Codes and programming: aware_bXX: 0 No; 1 Yes. Include recognised spontaneous or CEP recalls. If a brand was named earlier but not selected now, clarify neutrally before finalising. aware_none is exclusive. Keep resolved recognition separate from the original open responses.

evidence.text: Codes and programming: main_brand 1–10; 96 Other. Must be among O1 selections. Blank if no vehicle.
Response: 0–10 scale. Ask: main_brand is tracked brand.
I2 How likely would you be to recommend [MAIN BRAND] to someone choosing a vehicle?
following: Response: 0–10 scale. Ask: main_brand is tracked brand.

Codes and programming: 0 Not at all likely through 10 Extremely likely; 99 Do not know. Optional NPS extension. Do not combine with image pick-any questions. NPS=(%9–10)-(%0–6), known-score main-brand-user base.

coverage.note: I2 refers to MAIN BRAND, not an overall company or channel CSM battery.

evidence.text: A1 When you think of passenger car brands available in South Africa, which brand comes to mind first?
following: Response: Open text. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: Record verbatim before any names are shown. Code to brand registry; 96 Other named brand; 98 None. Do not correct or suggest brands.

evidence.text: A2 What other passenger car brands come to mind? Please name any others you can think of.
following: Response: Open text with multiple mentions. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: Record verbatim and code every distinct brand. Derive unaided_bXX including A1 and A2. No fixed minimum. 0 Not recalled; 1 Recalled for each tracked brand.

evidence.text: A3 Before today, which of these brands had you heard of?
following: Response: Multiple response brand list. Ask: all eligible.

Codes and programming: aware_bXX: 0 No; 1 Yes. Include recognised spontaneous or CEP recalls. If a brand was named earlier but not selected now, clarify neutrally before finalising. aware_none is exclusive. Keep resolved recognition separate from the original open responses.

evidence.text: F1 If you were choosing your next vehicle, which of these brands would you consider buying or leasing?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: all eligible; show recognised brands.
Codes and programming: consider_bXX: 0 Not considered; 1 Considered. None allowed. These are intentions at the interview, not observed future purchases.

evidence.text: F2 Which of those brands would make your serious shortlist?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: F1 has any selected brand; show only F1 selections.
Codes and programming: shortlist_bXX: 0 No; 1 Yes. Allow no shortlist yet. Do not force a top three.

evidence.text: F3 Which one of your shortlisted brands would be your first choice?
following: Response: Single response. Ask: F2 has any selected brand.

Codes and programming: Brand code 1–10; 98 No first choice yet. Derive firstchoice_bXX. Nested funnel: awareness >= consideration >= shortlist >= first choice. Not a longitudinal conversion or causal probability.

coverage.note: O4 repeat_bXX asks prior household acquisition only among brands acquired in the last 12 months. It is not an all-respondent ever-used/trial grid.
No per-brand past-week/month/3-month/6-month use grid. Do not substitute current ownership or acquisition.

evidence.text: O1 Which brands of vehicle does your household currently own or lease?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: owner_bXX 0/1; owner_other 0/1; owner_none exclusive. Verify recognition for any owned brand.

evidence.text: O3 Which brands has your household bought or started leasing in the past 12 months?
following: Response: Multiple response. Ask: S3=1.

Codes and programming: bought12_bXX 0/1; bought12_other 0/1. Rest of sample gets structural zero for derived all-sample indicators. Record asked route in S3. Acquisition can be new, used or lease, not a national new-car sales estimate.

coverage.note: bought12_b01–b10 / O3 is past-12-month acquisition, not usage or ownership over that window. owner_b01–b10 / O1 is current ownership.

evidence.text: AD1 Which car brands, if any, have you seen or heard advertising for in the past four weeks?
following: Response: Open text with multiple mentions. Ask: all eligible.

Codes and programming: Record verbatim, code ad_unaided_bXX 0/1. This occurs after brand recognition, so label it unprompted advertising recall after brand-list exposure, not uncontaminated top-of-mind awareness.

evidence.text: AD2 In the past four weeks, have you seen or heard any advertising for each of these brands?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Yes; 0 No; 9 Not sure. Blank if unaware. Derive adrecall_bXX all-sample 1 only for Yes, 0 otherwise. Report Not sure separately. Recall is not verified exposure or campaign effectiveness.

evidence.text: W1 Thinking about what other people have said about [BRAND] in the past four weeks, what have you heard?
following: Response: Single response per brand grid. Ask: recognised brands.

Codes and programming: 1 Mainly positive; 2 Mainly negative; 3 A mixture of positive and negative; 4 Neutral comments; 5 Have not heard people talk about it. Blank if unaware. Retain all five categories; do not disguise mixed or neutral as not heard.

evidence.text: P1 Which of the following have you used in the past seven days?
following: Response: Multiple response checklist. Ask: all eligible.
Codes and programming: One binary variable per medium; None exclusive. This is personal media use, not advertising exposure or a channel-effectiveness metric.

evidence.text: S1 How old are you?
following: Response: Numeric. Ask: all.
Codes and programming: 18–69 eligible. Record exact age and derive age band. Otherwise end.

evidence.text: Codes and programming: 18–69 eligible. Record exact age and derive age band. Otherwise end.

following: Response: Single response. Ask: all eligible.

following: Response: Single response. Ask: S3=1.

evidence.text: Codes and programming: main_brand 1–10; 96 Other. Must be among O1 selections. Blank if no vehicle.

following: Response: 0–10 scale. Ask: main_brand is tracked brand.

Codes and programming: 0 Not at all likely through 10 Extremely likely; 99 Do not know. Optional NPS extension. Do not combine with image pick-any questions. NPS=(%9–10)-(%0–6), known-score main-brand-user base.

coverage.note: I2 refers to MAIN BRAND, not an overall company or channel CSM battery.

evidence.text: Measure the most recent experience in each channel used during the past 30 days. Use this questionnaire with the three Channel wave files. One row represents one customer and one used channel in one wave. Overall company ratings are collected in the separate Company questionnaire.

Screen current customers for channel use in the past 30 days, then repeat the experience questions for each selected channel. Customers with no recent channel use contribute no experience rows. If linked to the Company tracker, carry forward respondent_id, wave, company, demographics and tenure instead of asking them again. The linked demonstration uses the same 1,000 customers per sector per wave.

The historical Ask Afrika Word attachment is a general questionnaire template with several unrelated examples, not a CSM-specific instrument. Its question/routing conventions inform the format. The earlier workbook supplies the company/call-centre split, IVR, process audit, service drivers and loyalty concepts. Neither file is overwritten.
Codes and programming: Age 18–69 and current service required. Record main company code and stable anonymous text respondent_id. No names, accounts, policy or phone numbers.

evidence.text: Measure the most recent experience in each channel used during the past 30 days. Use this questionnaire with the three Channel wave files. One row represents one customer and one used channel in one wave. Overall company ratings are collected in the separate Company questionnaire.

Screen current customers for channel use in the past 30 days, then repeat the experience questions for each selected channel. Customers with no recent channel use contribute no experience rows. If linked to the Company tracker, carry forward respondent_id, wave, company, demographics and tenure instead of asking them again. The linked demonstration uses the same 1,000 customers per sector per wave.

The historical Ask Afrika Word attachment is a general questionnaire template with several unrelated examples, not a CSM-specific instrument. Its question/routing conventions inform the format. The earlier workbook supplies the company/call-centre split, IVR, process audit, service drivers and loyalty concepts. Neither file is overwritten.
Codes and programming: Age 18–69 and current service required. Record main company code and stable anonymous text respondent_id. No names, accounts, policy or phone numbers.
Main company
S2 Which company do you use most, and how long have you used it?
following: Response: Single response and numeric. Ask: current customers.

important_distinctions: A provider identity is not a brand awareness battery.
Current ownership is not recent use; acquisition in the past 12 months is not usage or 12-month ownership.
Company ratings cannot be inferred from a channel record, or vice versa.
CSM Relationship rows are customers; Channel rows are recent experiences and may repeat the same customer.
ConnectMobile instrument is reconstructed; original rating anchors and recall periods remain unverified.

Tenure/retention intention is not an observed retention outcome.
